newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria oil funding meeting postponed again.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria oil funding meeting postponed again.

text.p: A meeting between Nigeria's joint venture oil production partners and senior government officials to discuss a funding crisis was on Wednesday put off for a second time, the oil ministry said.

An oil ministry spokesman told Reuters the meeting had been postponed because other government agencies, including the finance ministry, planning ministry and presidential advisory committee were not ready.
"We were ready to enter discussions so that funding of oil operations can go ahead but the others were not. Right now I cannot say when any meeting will take place," the spokesman said.
The meeting was originally scheduled to take place two weeks ago.

Oil industry officials say Nigeria's current production, of more than two million barrels per day, could be cut by as much as five percent in 1997 if an increase to their funding is not approved. They say long term effects would be even more serious.

The joint venture partners complain they have been forced to cut back new projects, maintenance and exploration after an across the board cut to $2.05 billion from a proposed $3.32 billion budget for 1997.
State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation owns an average 57 percent stake in joint-ventures with Royal Dutch/Shell, Mobil Corp, Chevron Corp, Elf Aquitaine, Texaco and Agip.
